record.paper_title: Open questions and perspectives for hadron electromagnetic form factors in space-like and time-like regions.
record.context_brief: Completeness and precision of radiative corrections
record.original_question: Can a complete and sufficiently precise calculation of radiative corrections, including all contributions and interference terms and their effects on electric and magnetic contributions to the reduced cross section, be developed for elastic electron-proton form-factor measurements so that Rosenbluth cross-section extractions and polarization-ratio measurements can be interpreted consistently at large Q^2?

evidence.quote: At large Q2 the Rosenbluth method is not very effective for the extraction of GE, essentially for two reasons: the contribution of the electric term to the cross section becomes very small, as the magnetic part is amplified by the kinematical factor τ, and radiative corrections, which should be applied to the data, can reach 30-40%.

Note that radiative corrections are not applied to the polarization results, as they are assumed to cancel in the polarization ratio [27], although a complete calculation of all contributions and their interference does not exist.
The extraction of GE from the unpolarized data requires a large precision in the calculation of radiative corrections, and in the procedure used to apply to the data.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider elastic electron–proton scattering, $e^- p \to e^- p$, parametrized by the squared four-momentum transfer $Q^2 = -q^2 > 0$. In the one-photon-exchange (Born) approximation, the unpolarized cross section is the Rosenbluth formula
$$\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega} = \left(\frac{d\sigma}{d\Omega}\right)_{\text{Mott}}\frac{1}{\varepsilon(1+\tau)}\Big[\tau\, G_M^2(Q^2) + \varepsilon\, G_E^2(Q^2)\Big],$$
where $\tau = Q^2/(4M_p^2)$, $\varepsilon$ is the virtual-photon longitudinal polarization, and $G_E, G_M$ are the proton electric and magnetic Sachs form factors. The ratio $G_E/G_M$ can be measured (i) via a Rosenbluth (longitudinal–transverse) separation of the reduced cross section, or (ii) via polarization-transfer experiments that measure the ratio of recoil-proton transverse to longitudinal polarizations.

At large $Q^2$ the electric contribution to the unpolarized cross section is kinematically suppressed relative to the magnetic one, and the experimentally applied radiative corrections (real and virtual photon emission, vacuum polarization, soft and hard two-photon exchange, lepton–proton bremsstrahlung interference, etc.) reach magnitudes of order $30$–$40\%$. In standard practice, radiative corrections are not applied to the polarization-transfer extraction under the assumption that they cancel in the polarization ratio, even though no complete calculation of all such contributions and their mutual interferences has been performed.

Problem. Develop a complete and quantitatively controlled calculation of the radiative corrections to elastic $ep$ scattering — including all contributions and their interference terms, and tracking separately their effects on the electric and magnetic pieces of the reduced cross section as well as on the polarization observables — such that:
(a) the Rosenbluth extraction of $G_E/G_M$ and the polarization-transfer extraction of $G_E/G_M$ become consistent at large $Q^2$;
(b) the non-cancellation of radiative effects in the polarization ratio is quantified;
(c) the residual theoretical uncertainty is small compared to the experimental precision of current and planned measurements.
Either construct such a calculation, or prove obstructions to its existence within QED plus a controlled hadronic model.
artifact.status_search_result: The discrepancy between Rosenbluth and polarization-transfer extractions of the proton form factor ratio at large Q^2 is widely attributed to two-photon-exchange and related higher-order radiative corrections, but as of 2024 a complete calculation including all interference terms is not available. Recent dedicated experiments (OLYMPUS at DESY, CLAS12, VEPP-3) confirm a small TPE effect at moderate Q^2 but do not validate theoretical treatments at large Q^2, and the proposed TPEX experiment aims to extend the kinematic range. Theory and experiment in this area remain active, and the question is regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Two-Photon Exchange in Elastic Electron-Proton Scattering | Jefferson Lab
status_evidence.snippet: The discrepancy in the form factor ratio has not been resolved and the role played by two-photon exchange continues to be widely discussed.
status_evidence.claim: The Rosenbluth/polarization-transfer discrepancy and the role of TPE radiative corrections remain unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The two-photon exchange experiment at DESY
status_evidence.snippet: Results support a small two-photon exchange effect but at larger momentum transfers theory remains untested.
status_evidence.claim: Theoretical treatments of TPE corrections remain untested at large Q^2 as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: A measurement of two-photon exchange in Super-Rosenbluth separations with positron beams
status_evidence.snippet: Further measurements and theoretical work on two-photon exchange on the proton form factors are clearly needed.
status_evidence.claim: Further theoretical work on complete radiative corrections is still needed.
